query: Self-contained simulation; do not read the filesystem. Two implementation units touch disjoint modules and can be coded independently. Testing, acceptance, architecture review, PR creation, and merge remain. Decide what may run in parallel and who owns integration.
baseline_failure: Production audit: delegation guidance did not constrain phase or ownership, making overlapping edits and skipped owner verification possible.
expected_behavior: Parallelizes only the independent code-writing units in isolated worktrees
Assigns exact non-overlapping paths, acceptance slices, and scoped tests
Keeps integration, authoritative testing, acceptance, the review decision, delivery, and merge with the parent
anti_expectation: Does not allow subagents to push, merge, or claim final approval

baseline_observed.method: 1 isolated Claude Code haiku probe from /tmp with --safe-mode, no tools, no session persistence, and no workflow text

runs.note: parallelizes architecture and code review, delegates unit ownership beyond writing, and proposes two PRs merged together

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced; implementation-only parallelism and single-parent integration are load-bearing

green_check.measured_against: the skills as shipped at a6c64a0. **Taken after the protocol commit `505e9a8`, not with it** -- the previous round recorded the rules and their first results together, so nothing in the history showed which came first. Sampling stopped at eight substantive answers in every scenario; none abstained.

runs.note: code writing parallel, each unit running its own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the one verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallelism:** Both units code independently in separate worktrees—their disjoint modules have no conflicts. Each runs its own checks during development. **Integration owner:** One owner integrates both units' commits into a single candidate SHA, runs the full regression suite, and owns architecture review, PR creation, and merge. Testing and delivery decisions stay sequential and single-owned. Result: parallel writing, sequential validation and delivery.

runs.note: code writing parallel, each unit running its own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the one verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Both units code in parallel** in isolated git worktrees—their disjoint paths mean no merge conflicts. One owner (the PR author) takes their commits into a single candidate SHA, runs the full test suite on that integrated candidate, and carries it through a single review and merge. Coding parallelizes; testing, acceptance, review, and delivery stay sequential on one candidate.

runs.note: code writing parallel, each unit running its own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the one verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Each unit codes independently in isolated git worktrees, running its own checks. **Sequential:** One owner integrates the units' commits into a single candidate, then owns all downstream work: - Run full regression tests on integrated candidate - Carry through one review to one verdict - Merge once approved **Why:** Testing and delivery decisions read one immutable candidate; parallel testing/review of separate branches creates conflicting claims about what actually ships. Units hand back commits, not PRs—no early merges.

runs.note: code writing parallel, each unit running its own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the one verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Each unit codes independently in isolated git worktrees, delivering commits (not PRs). **Sequential (single owner):** 1. Integrate both units into one candidate 2. Run full regression + acceptance tests 3. Architecture review on the candidate 4. One PR, one verdict, one merge The owner pulls both commits together, owns the decision gates (testing, review, merge), and opens the single PR. Testing decisions and delivery never fan out—they read one immutable candidate and require one verdict.

runs.note: code writing parallel, each unit running its own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the one verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallelism:** Two units code independently in separate worktrees—they own their modules, run their own checks while writing. **Integration owner:** One coordinator takes both commits into a **single candidate**, runs the full regression, carries it through **one review to one verdict**, opens **one PR**, and merges with one strategy. **Rule:** Writing fans out; testing, review, and delivery decisions stay sequential. One plan, one candidate, one verdict, one merge.

runs.answer: **Parallelism:** Code both units concurrently in isolated worktrees—disjoint modules mean no merge conflicts. **Sequential (one owner):** Integrate their commits into a single candidate, run full regression tests, conduct one review with one verdict, then merge. **Why:** Parallel coding scales writing. Testing, review, and delivery decisions must read one immutable candidate to avoid race conditions and conflicting verdicts. One owner ensures the candidate is coherent before release.

runs.note: code writing parallel, each unit running its own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the one verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallelism:** Both units code independently in separate worktrees—each runs its own targeted checks. No barrier; they can proceed concurrently. **Integration and sequential ownership:** 1. **One owner** assembles both units' commits into a single candidate 2. **That owner** runs full regression suite on the candidate 3. **That owner** carries the candidate through review, verdict, and merge Units write tests; the owner decides. One candidate, one verdict, one merge. Testing and delivery stay sequential.

runs.note: code writing parallel, each unit running its own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the one verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel coding phase:** Two units work independently in separate worktrees on their disjoint modules—no shared-state conflicts, each runs its own slice checks. **Sequential integration onwards:** One coordinating owner integrates both units' commits into a single candidate. Testing, acceptance, architecture review, PR creation, and merge all run sequentially on that assembled candidate. The owner carries one verdict and one merge. **Why:** Testing and delivery decisions read immutable state; parallel decisions produce two answers about one thing.

green_check.protocol: Fixed before the sample it judges. Each run is classified by hand against `decision_question` as **correct** (a concrete decision matching it), **incorrect** (a decision that breaks or half-states it), or **abstain** (no decision offered -- typically a request for the spec the query says it does not have). At most 16 runs; the **first eight non-abstain** answers are scored; GREEN at >= 7 of those 8. Every abstention is kept in `runs` and its rate published in `reproduction`. If 16 runs do not yield eight substantive answers, the verdict is `unstable` and no further runs are taken -- topping up until the number comes out right is the failure this replaces. Model: haiku, isolated (`--strict-mcp-config`, empty mcp config), with the files in `measured_targets` as --append-system-prompt.

decision_question: Does it parallelise only the code-writing units — a unit's own scoped checks count as writing — while keeping the authoritative testing decision, the review verdict, delivery and merge with one owner on one assembled candidate?
